TOOL_ACT3_SCENE02_CBS.instructions: Review the auto-summed cost of every task from the WBS. If the total exceeds the threshold, you must cut one task.
TOOL_ACT3_SCENE02_CBS.descopeRule: If the sum of all included tasks (from WBS) exceeds descopeThreshold, the player must select exactly one task to cut before continuing. Cutting a task sets a flag: descoped_<taskId> = true, and removes its cost from the total. The cut task becomes a real, trackable gap (e.g. cutting wbs_operator_training should weaken team readiness later, same pattern as the risk-investigation skipped-dimension consequences).
TOOL_ACT3_SCENE02_CBS.completionCondition: Total is at or below descopeThreshold (via descope if needed)

TOOL_ACT3_SCENE06_BENEFITS.instructions: For each benefit, build the full proof chain: Measure, Evidence, Owner, When Measurable.

measureTensionMoment.reaction: Meetings don't secure a contract. Nothing's real until it's signed.
measureTensionMoment.note: Activity vs. outcome, same lesson as the patients-treated tension moment: attending meetings is work toward the goal, not proof the goal happened.

evidenceTensionMoment.reaction: A status report says the deal's coming. Procurement's paperwork says it's done.
evidenceTensionMoment.note: Deliberately tempting: Mike E.'s monthly written report is a real mechanic set up in ACT3_SCENE05 and paid off in ACT4_SCENE05, so a player who's been paying attention may reach for it here — it's a real artifact, just not the primary source. Procurement's own signed records are.

measureTensionMoment.marcusLine: Can't we just measure success by the facility being open?
measureTensionMoment.camilleLine: Opening a facility doesn't mean we've delivered anything. Nobody's been treated yet.
measureTensionMoment.reaction: Facility completion tells you the building's finished. It doesn't tell you anyone's been treated.
measureTensionMoment.note: Player picks between the two, learning outputs (facility exists) vs. outcomes (patients actually treated). No penalty for picking wrong, but a correcting reaction line, same as the PESTLE tool-selection pattern.

evidenceTensionMoment.reaction: The validation certificate says the line works. It doesn't say anyone's used it yet.
evidenceTensionMoment.note: Tempting because the player just spent an entire earlier scene (IQ/OQ, in the WBS) earning this artifact — it's real, it's just evidence the equipment functions, not evidence patients are being treated.

measureTensionMoment.reaction: Revenue alone doesn't tell Daniel if it was worth twelve million. ROI weighs it against what was spent.
measureTensionMoment.note: Classic finance near-miss: revenue sounds like the obvious answer to 'was it worth it', but it ignores the cost side of the question Daniel is actually asking.

evidenceTensionMoment.reaction: A forecast is a guess about what might happen. Daniel wants what actually did.
evidenceTensionMoment.note: Projected vs. actual, echoing correctWhen's '12 months after go-live' — a forecast is exactly the kind of thing that would be available too early and wouldn't hold up to Daniel's question.

TOOL_ACT4_SCENE05_STATUS_REPORT.note: Upcoming Milestones and completed-milestone accomplishment candidates are both derived at render time from TOOL_ACT3_SCENE04_MILESTONES's real placements (see ganttToolId) split against the current week -- never hardcoded here. Upcoming Activities is likewise derived at render time: for each Gantt milestone in progress or starting within upcomingActivityWindowWeeks of the current week, its individual WBS task cards (see wbsToolId, matched by milestone.wbsCategory == card.correctBucket) become separate checkable activity items -- a finer-grained, real, near-term breakdown rather than the milestone's own single headline title. upcomingActivityCandidates is a fallback only, shown if that real data produces nothing (e.g. before any milestone has been placed). See StatusReportBuilder.tsx.
